headline: Radio waves carry sound through walls, across oceans, and into space—completely invisible
universal_truth: What we can't see can still profoundly affect us; invisible forces shape our world
fun_facts: Radio waves travel at the speed of light—they could circle Earth seven times in one second
Your body is constantly being passed through by radio signals—WiFi, cell signals, FM broadcasts
The first transatlantic radio message was sent in 1901, stunning a world used to telegraph wires
discussion_questions: How did wireless communication change human connection?
What invisible signals are passing through you right now?
How do we trust information from invisible sources?

hook.script: Right now, invisible waves are passing through your body carrying music, conversations, and data. Radio waves move at the speed of light, pass through walls, and connect devices without any visible link. We live immersed in invisible signals.

cliff.script: Sound is vibration in air. Radio waves are electromagnetic. How can vibrating air become an invisible wave that travels through the vacuum of space where there's no air to vibrate?
cliff.prompt: How does sound travel on radio waves?

options.text: Sound is encoded onto radio waves—the wave carries information about the sound, not the sound itself
options.response: Yes. Radio waves carry a pattern representing the sound. Your radio decodes that pattern and recreates the vibrations as sound your ears can hear.

options.text: Radio waves are a higher-frequency form of sound that travels through anything
options.response: Radio waves aren't sound—they're electromagnetic. They carry information that gets converted back to sound...

fact1.title: Encoded Information
fact1.script: Radio waves don't carry actual sound—they carry patterns that represent sound. A microphone converts air vibrations to electrical signals, which modulate the radio wave. Your receiver reverses the process: wave to electrical signal to speaker vibration to sound.

fact2.title: Electromagnetic Family
fact2.script: Radio waves are part of the electromagnetic spectrum—the same family as light, X-rays, and microwaves. They're all made of the same thing, just different frequencies. Radio waves are simply light we can't see, tuned to carry information.

fact3.title: Wireless Revolution
fact3.script: Before radio, messages required physical connection—wires or messengers. When Marconi sent a signal across the Atlantic in 1901, the world changed. Communication could happen without any visible link. The wireless age began.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What we can't see can profoundly affect us. Radio waves prove that invisible forces shape our world. Just because something is invisible doesn't mean it's not real—or not important.

outro.script: That's Day 124. Tomorrow, we'll explore talking across distances—communication technology. Until then, consider the invisible signals constantly passing through you and around you.

growTrack.title: Invisible Awareness - Sense the Unseen
growTrack.learning_objective: Appreciate the invisible infrastructure around you
growTrack.activity: Turn on a radio or stream music wirelessly. Consider: this audio traveled to you on invisible waves, passing through walls and space. Count how many wireless signals you're using today: WiFi, Bluetooth, cellular. You're immersed in invisible communication.
